attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own Substack post, describing his own Fortune essay.

semantics.note: 'Might' hedges only whether the essay explains the situation. The underlying claim, that success has been elusive in many applications despite about $500B invested, is stated as fact. 'In many applications' is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: 'many' does not mean 'most', and success is read broadly. Using 2024 as the window was the evaluator's choice but is reasonable. The investment basis was not stated, so the result depends on how cumulative investment is scoped.

evidence.note: Original PwC survey from before publication. Only about a third of CEOs reported revenue or profit gains, and results fell below expectations. This partly supports the claim of widespread difficulty, but it measures companies, not applications, and gives no investment total.

Deloitte survey (Jul–Sep 2024) reports positive ROI for organizations' most advanced initiatives and says scaling remains a challenge. This limits a story of broad failure but does not disprove difficulty in many other applications.

Stanford AI Index: $33.9B of private genAI investment in 2024. That is one year of private funding, a different metric from cumulative total investment, so it neither verifies nor refutes the ~$500B figure.

reviews.rationale: The support condition requires both widespread application difficulty and an accounting that shows about $500B already invested. PwC gives partial support for difficulty, and Deloitte qualifies it. No item in the packet establishes or refutes a cumulative ~$500B total; the AI Index figure covers a different, narrower metric. The packet does not settle the claim, so it is unresolved.
